title: Book One · Chapter 66: Two Kinds of Work
story:
Mum has three pairs of trousers on the table.

One pair needs a shorter leg. One needs a new button. The third pair has a hole. The hole looks like a little smiling mouth.

Ronan points at it. “That one is happy.”

“That one will keep me busy all afternoon,” Mum says.

She holds a piece of dark cloth behind the hole. It is not quite the same colour. She puts it aside and tries another piece.

“Can I help?”

“You can put these buttons in the small tin. The loose ones, not the ones still on the card.”

He begins. There are white buttons and brown buttons. There are two red ones too. Another looks black at first. Ronan holds it in the light to look again.

“Are you going to get lots of money?”

“Some money. Not lots.”

“How much for the happy trousers?”

Mum tells him. The pay is less than he expected. The work takes a whole afternoon.

“Then do the button pair first.”

“I said the hole would be ready today. The button pair is for tomorrow.”

Ronan rolls a red button across the table. Mum stops it with one finger before it falls.

“You are doing my work very fast,” she says. “Where is your own?”

His reading sheet is under the buttons.

He pulls it out. At school he said, “I can read the whole page.” Leo read one line aloud. Ronan remembers the sound of it. Now he cannot read two words in the middle.

Mum goes back to the cloth. Ronan reads the first two lines quietly. At the third, he stops.

“Is this near or next?”

“Show me.”

She looks. “Near.”

He reads again. It still takes effort. Mum turns her chair a little so her elbow does not cover his page.

For a while, they do their different work at the same table.

A woman comes for the trousers before the hole is finished. Mum shows her the cloth on the inside.

“It will be strong,” she says. “The outside will still show a little.”

The woman looks closely.

“That is all right for work. I do not need them for a wedding.”

Mum laughs and asks her to come back before supper. She does not promise to hide the hole completely.

When the woman leaves, Ronan reads his page aloud. He makes one mistake, goes back and reads the line again.

“That sounds clearer,” Mum says.

“Are you listening?”

“Yes. I can hear you while I sew.”

He likes that. She can sew and listen at the same time.

At the end, he puts a small mark beside the difficult line. Tomorrow he will read it again before school.

Dad comes in to wash before his evening meal. Ronan wants him to hear the difficult line too. Dad holds his wet hands over the bowl and listens.

“Good,” he says.

“You did not look.”

“I was listening.”

Ronan makes him look as well. Dad dries one finger. Dad points below the words. His finger stays just above the paper. Ronan reads more slowly this time, but he gets through the line.

Mum finishes sewing the hole closed. It no longer looks like a smiling mouth. She turns the trousers over and presses the cloth flat with her palm.

“Now they look serious,” Ronan says.

“They have work to do.”

He closes the button tin. The two red buttons knock together inside. He leaves them there and carries his own finished page to his bag.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- pairs of＝几条／几双
- not quite＝不完全
- goes back＝回头重做
- while＝在……同时

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：wedding＝婚礼；sew＝缝；palm＝手掌。

## 读句提示

**She can sew and listen at the same time.**

她能／一边缝衣一边听。and连接两个动作。

## 理解问题

1. Mum为什么不先做最简单的裤子？
2. Ronan在阅读上遇到了什么真实困难？
